KS2 Roman Adventure Stunning Start - 6th September 2013
We were taken back to Roman times with the visit of `Lucius' a Roman soldier. He told us all about what life had been like in the Roman army; about the different ranks of soldiers and what was required to become a Roman soldier - so many interesting facts to take on board. We were then put through our paces and learnt about the different battle formations ...

KS2 Storms & Shipwrecks Stunning Start - 6th January 2014
KS2 became ship designers and builders for the day as part of the stunning start to their new topic - Storms and Shipwrecks.
The pupils worked in mixed year groups to research and learn about their choice of ship from whatever era they wanted. They were then tasked with building a model of their ship and were also asked to be ready to explain their decision making on their design features.
It was a very industrious time and there were many fantastic creations ...

KS2 Stunning Start - Walkabout Australia - 5th September 2014
KS2 were given a big clue to their new topic this term with a fabulous aboriginal style mural in the school hall. Mr Poole introduced the new topic - Walkabout Australia - by telling them a little about Australia; showing them where it is in the world; describing some of the well known places of interest and pointing out how some of the language differs!
The children were then put in mixed aged groups and they set off on one of many activities for the day. Each group spent time bridge building, maybe using the Sydney Harbour bridge for inspiration! They then produced their own piece of aboriginal art and enjoyed the fine weather honing their cricket skills on the sports field, as well as working as a team producing their own poster on Australian facts.

French Skipping Workshop - 5th November 2014
A company called 'Small Earth Games' came in to teach us different french skipping games. Each class spent time during the day learning a skipping game and the day culminated with everyone coming together for a demonstration of what had been learnt. The playground is now littered with children playing the newly learnt games including `England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales', the ladder game and the kanagaroo game!
Great fun was had by all.

Smartphone Free Childhood Campaign
Tunbridge Wells Primary School Smartphone Free letter
Below is a letter outlining the agreement and expectations from September 2026 regarding personal smartphones, smartwatches or other internet enabled devices within school. This has been formed between many of the local primary schools in Tunbridge Wells and aligns Speldhurst with the coordinated smartphone-free policy being introduced across Tunbridge Wells secondary schools.
When children first started getting smartphones a decade ago, there was little research about this impact. Now there is, and it’s overwhelming.
At Speldhurst Primary School, we understand the challenges faced by parents to keep children safe online. Our children live in a world of instant access and there is growing concern regarding the use of mobile phones and the exposure to things that a child’s brain may not be developed enough to deal with.
In the UK, there is a campaign supporting and guiding parents to create a ‘SmartPhone Free Childhood.’
The campaign highlights the growing concern that ‘when we give our children access to the whole world in their pocket, we give the whole world access to our children.’ (The problem — Smartphone Free Childhood)
We wish to share the following information to our school community.
Please follow the below link for a webinar run by Jenny Byrne – Kent regional leader for the Smartphone Free Childhood Campaign - who is also a child and adolescent psychotherapist. It also includes guest speakers Joanna Pringle and the Head Teacher of John Wallis Church of England Academy, who has implemented a Smartphone Free School.

KS1 Fire Engine Visit - 2nd October 2015
As part of their topic, 'Fire, Fire', Pippin and Galaxy Gala pupils were so excited to receive a visit from a working fire engine and crew. Sirens wailed, hoses were filled and Mrs Rose and Mrs Perry were transformed into fire fighters!
What a wonderful time everyone had ...
